Dependabot dependency updates fail the changelog gate because the bot cannot write fragments. Python tool updates also leave the executable zizmor version behind the audited requirement. This PR removes both causes and reports dependency PRs that remain open past their review budget.

Fixes #28

## Changes

- Pass `github.event.pull_request.user.login` into the changelog checker and exempt exactly `dependabot[bot]`. Human PRs still need fragments even when their branch starts with `dependabot/` or the workflow actor is a bot. Both repository layouts are covered.
- Read the zizmor spec from `scripts/requirements-security.txt` in both pipx audit passes and the local reproduction instructions. Preserve the regular and pedantic audit policies. Requirements changes now trigger the Workflows checks; a missing pin fails before running pipx.
- Add a daily (07:23 UTC) and manually triggered **Dependabot Health** workflow with read-only contents/PR permissions, job timeouts, concurrency and the standard Pipeline Status gate. It paginates all open PRs and fails with links and remediation when a Dependabot PR is older than 14 days, regardless of CI status or recent rebases. `DEPENDABOT_MAX_OPEN_DAYS` sets a positive custom budget; `CI_VERBOSE=true` enables age diagnostics. API/configuration failures fail explicitly, and PR text is escaped in annotations.
- Document the exception, release behavior, version source and health configuration. Add a patch fragment; the existing release pipeline bumps the version on merge.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

The original logs confirm the failures:

- [Run 43402801047](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43402801047): missing changelog fragment and `Unaudited workflow tool: zizmor==1.31.1` after the manifest moves to 1.32.0.
- [Run 43402827872](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43402827872): missing changelog fragment for the action update.

The nine new changelog/workflow regression cases **fail before the fix**. The focused suite **passes 134 tests** afterward:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  scripts/tests/test_changelog.py \
  scripts/tests/test_workflows.py \
  scripts/tests/test_check_dependabot_health.py \
  scripts/tests/test_check_workflow_concurrency.py
```

The workflow tests execute both real shell commands with a fake pipx and simulate manifest changes to 1.32.0 and a future version. Health tests freeze time and cover the exact age boundary, custom limits, recently rebased old PRs, a match beyond the first API page, human/closed PR exclusions, API errors, malformed responses, and command-injection escaping.

Local concurrency policy, required documentation, file-size and diff checks pass. A live read-only health check enumerated #26 and #27; both are younger than the 14-day limit. Full compiler, packaging, security and link checks run in CI to avoid duplicating expensive builds locally.

Final-commit CI is **green** for `0f2bfc3ef05e7be9518229f712998c317b9b9fa8`: all five workflows completed successfully, including every Pipeline Status gate. The full release-script suite passed **503 tests**.

- [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540045611): GCC, Clang, Apple Clang and MSVC, sanitizers, coverage, lint, changelog/version checks, fresh-merge simulation, 503 script tests and package/consumer validation.
- [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540045623): both CodeQL scans, full dependency audits and dependency review.
- [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540045646): actionlint, concurrency policy and both zizmor audit passes.
- [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540045633) and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43540045669).

Final review confirms the latest `main` is included, the working tree is clean, the full PR diff preserves existing features, and GitHub recognizes the closing reference for #28.

The scheduled workflow will become available on the default branch after merge; its script and workflow policies are verified before merge. Existing Dependabot PRs receive the new base-branch behavior after rebasing onto the merged fix. No bot branches are modified by this PR.

[Investigation and requirement evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-28-1a8274155c0d/docs/case-studies/issue-28/README.md).

Bumps the ci-tools group with 2 updates in the /scripts directory: [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor) and [clang-format](https://github.com/ssciwr/clang-format-wheel). Updates `zizmor` from 1.31.1 to 1.32.0
Release notes

Sourced from zizmor's releases.

v1.32.0

Sponsorship is appreciated!

New Features 🌈🔗

  • zizmor now has experimental support for GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles. Please see the limitations documentation for more information about the current implementation and its limitations (#2463)

Enhancements 🌱🔗

  • zizmor's input collection is now "root-aware" by default, meaning that invocations like zizmor . will no longer collect inputs unless they would actually be used by GitHub Actions, etc. This should eliminate spurious findings from (e.g.) workflow definitions in vendored directories. See the input collection documentation for more information. (#2454)

  • zizmor's LSP now honors the didChangeWorkspaceFolders event (#2461)

  • zizmor's LSP now audits pre-commit inputs (#2485)

  • zizmor now provides Windows ARM64 wheels on PyPI (#2424)

    Many thanks to @​ndabas for proposing and implementing this improvement!

Bug Fixes 🐛🔗

  • Fixed a bug where the bot-conditions audit did not properly flag if: condition of jobs that call a reusable workflow (#2457)

  • Fixed a bug where the obfuscation audit would incorrectly flag (and suggest an incorrect auto-fix for) expressions that constant-reduce to other expressions (#2483)

  • Fixed a bug where the template-injection audit did not flag attacker-controllable contexts wrapped in fromJSON(...), such as fromJSON(toJSON(github.event.issue.title)) (#2495)

  • Fixed a bug where the template-injection audit did not flag attacker-controllable contexts in the values of case(...), such as case(cond, github.event.issue.title, 'x') (#2504)

  • Fixed a class of bugs in the obfuscation audit where a constant-reducible subexpression would not be replaced with a contextually correct form (#2483)

  • Fixed a bug where zizmor would incorrectly audit pre-commit inputs that ended with .yml, despite pre-commit requiring the .yaml suffix (#2485)

  • Fixed a bug where zizmor would not honor some ignore comments for the stale-action-refs audit (#2494)

  • Fixed a bug where zizmor would not honor some ignore comments for the ref-version-mismatch audit (#2494)

Requirements-only Dependabot PRs currently report a green pipeline while skipping the tools they upgrade. Native NuGet packages can also reach the final release push without a size check and fail deterministically with HTTP 413. This PR fixes both problems across the detector, packaging, PR validation, and both release modes.

Fixes #24
Fixes #22
Fixes #23

## Changes

- Recognize `requirements*.txt` within the C++ project and shared pipeline directories, preserving documentation/experiment and unrelated-language exclusions. Shared manifest changes also enable coverage and documentation validation.
- Include PR #21's exact CI/security tool upgrades so this PR exercises them. Align both executable zizmor workflow pins with the new audited version (1.31.1); the newly enabled policy test caught that mismatch. Use the documented direct CLI integration because the pinned action rejects the newer version; retain annotations, online auditing and both audit passes. Fix both benchmark loop values flagged by clang-tidy 23.1.4 by declaring them `const`. Correct two CodeQL version comments to `v4.39.1` after verifying their existing SHA against the release tag; the upgraded online auditor caught the stale `v4` labels. These were genuine failures hidden by the old skip behavior.
- Enforce `NUGET_MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES` (default **249,000,000 compressed bytes**) during native NuGet packing, before local push/restore in Build Packages, and immediately before release upload. One repository variable configures PRs and automatic/instant releases; local callers can use the environment variable.
- Reject oversized packages with a GitHub error annotation, the ten largest ZIP entries by compressed size, and guidance to reduce or split payloads. Accept exact-budget packages; fail closed on invalid/nonpositive settings or unreadable packages. Inspect metadata without extracting payloads.
- On a server HTTP 413 / `RequestEntityTooLarge`, stop after one push attempt, identify it as non-retryable, preserve the failing exit status, and prevent Conan/GitHub publication. Existing duplicate handling, dry runs and tagged-source publishing remain covered.
- Add patch release fragments; the existing release workflow performs the version bump on merge.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

At baseline 29d8cf2, `detect_code_changes.classify(["scripts/requirements-ci.txt", "scripts/requirements-security.txt"])` returns false for all gates. Packing/validating with a one-byte budget has no effect, and a stubbed 413 has no explicit permanent-failure diagnostic.

`python3 experiments/verify_issue_24_regressions.py` runs selected new tests against the original scripts and restores the working files: **11 regression cases fail before the fix**. They cover requirements-only PRs in both layouts, packing and restore gates, the independent pre-push gate, and both 413 formats. Small ZIP fixtures and mocked publishing commands avoid large allocations and real uploads.

Additional tests cover compressed byte boundaries, default/empty and invalid budgets, missing/corrupt packages, largest-entry ordering, ordinary upload failures, and shared workflow configuration. Existing script tests cover duplicate-safe uploads, disabled channels, dry runs, tagged sources and the GitHub-release-last ordering.

Validation: **455 local script tests passed** in 173.62 seconds using pytest 9.2.0. All five workflows pass on commit `198bf0a`: [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43401085332), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43401085350), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43401085292), [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43401085387), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43401085622). CI passes all 455 script tests, Linux GCC/Clang, Windows MSVC, macOS Apple Clang, sanitizers, coverage, CodeQL, upgraded tool audits, NuGet packing/restore, and the vcpkg consumer check. All 83 focused workflow/detector tests, both offline zizmor 1.31.1 audit passes, and the online regular audit also pass. Shell syntax, required-document checks, file-size checks, and `git diff --check` pass. Full C++ and distribution builds run in CI to avoid duplicating them locally.

PR #21's original run was rerun successfully (attempt 2) using `gh run rerun 42463434826`, and reproduced the skipped checks. Historical reruns use the original classifier; this PR's current-commit CI verifies that the upgraded tools actually execute with corrected gates.

## Analysis and alternatives

[Requirement-by-requirement analysis, implementation map, reproduction, and research](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-24-f6a5158cb3d6/docs/case-studies/issue-24/README.md) records the complete scope. Both bugs were reproducible and neither was already resolved.

Microsoft documents [an approximate 250 MB NuGet limit and HTTP 413](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/nuget-org/publish-a-package#package-size-limits), so the default uses conservative decimal bytes. Existing components considered: [dorny/paths-filter](https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter), Python's standard-library [zipfile metadata API](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipfile.html), and the related [platform-package split in hive-mind PR #4051](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/4051). Extending the existing classifier and reusing the standard library preserves multi-language behavior without adding dependencies or changing the package layout.

## Summary

Fixes #19.

If GitHub can't give a job a hosted runner ("The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts"; macOS arm64 is the usual case), the job ends `cancelled` or `failure` with no steps and an empty `runner_name`. Before this PR, that blocked **Build Packages** and **Auto Release**, turned **Pipeline Status** red as if the code were at fault, and nothing retried the job. This PR implements all three parts of the issue's suggested fix.

### 1. Automatic re-run of infrastructure failures (`.github/workflows/rerun-infrastructure-failures.yml`)
- Triggered by `workflow_run` when a **CI/CD Pipeline** run completes as `failure` or `cancelled`. It checks out only the default branch, runs nothing from the triggering run, and needs only `actions: write` and `checks: read`.
- `scripts/unacquired_jobs.py rerun` counts a job as unacquired only if **all** of these hold:
  - its conclusion is `cancelled` or `failure`
  - it has no steps and an empty `runner_name`
  - one of its check-run annotations contains "was not acquired by Runner"
- The annotation check goes beyond the issue's sketch. Queued jobs that a newer push or a person cancelled also end with no steps and no runner, and they must not be re-run. A job that ran steps is never re-run.
- Runs `gh run rerun <id> --failed` on attempts 1 and 2. `--failed` also re-runs the dependent jobs, so Build Packages, Auto Release and Pipeline Status are evaluated again. On attempt 3 the workflow fails with the manual command instead of looping.

### 2. Pipeline Status names the cause
- `check-pipeline-status.sh` still fails, because nothing was tested. It now also prints `::error title=Hosted runner not acquired::<jobs>. GitHub could not provide a runner, so no code ran…`.
- The `pipeline-status` job in `release.yml` gets `GH_TOKEN` plus `actions: read` and `checks: read`.
- The API is called only when the gate already fails. Without a token it does nothing, and API errors only produce a warning.

### 3. Optional non-blocking macOS leg
- When the repository variable `MACOS_NON_BLOCKING=true` is set, the macOS test leg uses `continue-on-error`. A final step then adds its own `Non-blocking macOS leg failed` warning, because `needs.test.result` reports success in that case.
- It is off by default, so macOS stays a blocking, supported platform.

Docs: a new section, `docs/ci-cd.md#runner-acquisition-failures`, plus the README variables table and a changelog fragment (patch).

## How to reproduce
Push to `main` while macOS hosted capacity is constrained, or point one matrix leg at an unavailable label. Before this PR, the gate turned red and stayed red until someone re-ran the job by hand. A real example is links-notation run 41477660740, job `kotlin / ios`.

## Verification
- `scripts/tests/test_unacquired_jobs.py` puts a fake `gh` on `PATH` and serves job and annotation JSON fixtures. It covers:
  - classification, including real failures and superseded queued jobs, which are never re-run
  - the attempt limit and the give-up message
  - the gate naming the cause
  - the gate staying quiet on real failures and successes
  - API errors and a missing token

  Against the original `check-pipeline-status.sh`, the two gate tests fail; with this PR they pass.
- Full `pytest scripts/tests`: 428 passed. zizmor 1.29.0 reports no findings. actionlint 1.7.12 reports only the existing `queue:` lines, which CI comments out first.
- Live dry run against the real failed run from the issue: `experiments/check_unacquired_real_run.sh` → `Hosted runner not acquired::kotlin / ios (attempt 1)` and `Dry run: would run gh run rerun 41477660740 --failed --repo link-foundation/links-notation`.

## Notes
- The rerun workflow has its own Pipeline Status job, like every workflow in this template (enforced by `test_pipeline_status_needs_every_other_job`).
- `workflow_run` only fires for workflow files on the default branch, so the automatic re-run can't be exercised end to end until this PR is merged. The logic itself is covered by the offline tests and the live dry run above.

Preserve queued release/Pages writers, fix link checks that could retry without sleeping or accept a missing report, and make security findings affect the workflow's terminal result.

- All repository writers share `repository-main-write`, `cancel-in-progress: false` and `queue: max` (up to 100 waiting jobs). Pages configuration now runs inside its writer job. Read-only groups remain independent; bounded non-fast-forward recovery is preserved.
- Every active remote action uses a reviewed full commit SHA; Docker uses a digest. Dependabot remains enabled and zizmor has no namespace exceptions. A bounded compatibility step validates queue fields before commenting out only those lines for actionlint 1.7.12; all other syntax and shell checks remain enabled.
- Link retries use explicit round state and bounded backoff, including a single remaining URL. Missing lychee reports fail with `all_archived=false`; recovered transport errors cannot hide final HTTP/local errors or make archived live failures pass.
- C++ CodeQL traces the real C++20 release build, all consumer examples and the Conan package test in either repository layout. CodeQL retains SARIF and a mandatory validator rejects findings at every level, failed diagnostics, absent/unknown execution state and missing reports. Full Python and native audits run on PR, main, weekly and manual events independently of PR dependency review. Artifacts retain resolved direct/transitive coordinates and coverage verdicts; all enforcement jobs feed Pipeline Status.

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, research and verification evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-16-7c9fab3e69e0/docs/case-studies/issue-16/README.md) covers every requirement in the parent and all three required issues. The [action-pin inventory](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-16-7c9fab3e69e0/docs/case-studies/issue-16/action-pins.json) links reviewed upstream manifests. Existing components considered include native GitHub concurrency, actionlint/shellcheck, pip-audit, Conan Audit and OSV-Scanner; Conan's supported provider was selected to distinguish unknown packages from a covered clean result.

### Reproduction and regression coverage

- The baseline fails five link regressions, including the specified reset-then-200 case with `initial_wait_ms=1`; the fixed implementation sleeps exactly `0.001` seconds. Tests also cover multiple links collapsing to one, finite deadlines, missing versus valid empty reports, and mixed final HTTP failures.
- Workflow policy tests reproduce omitted queue fields and mutable actions. `experiments/check_actionlint_queue.py` accepts all current workflows and rejects invalid queues, quoted/inline forms, unrelated syntax errors and shellcheck errors without a broad diagnostic suppression. Literal/folded script strings, including YAML in shell heredocs, remain unchanged; three failing-before regressions cover this review finding.
- CI exposed an existing build-free C++ extraction failure: inferred C++17 left all five translation units incomplete. Four failing-before regressions cover manual build wiring, both layouts, consumer/package entry points and compiler failure. The explicit build passes locally; the SARIF gate remains strict. See [the failed security run](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40961167465), aggregate log line 4919 (C++ job log line 2280).
- Manual analysis then reported 68 successful extractions, zero extractor failures and 52 findings ([run 40963291575](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40963291575), C++ log lines 2620–2671). Both repository benchmark warnings are fixed with explicit discard expressions. The other 50 findings came from downloaded GoogleTest/Benchmark sources: pinned libraries are now built outside the checkout before tracing; all project sources remain traced with SYSTEM dependency headers. No SARIF results or diagnostics are filtered or suppressed. Four failing-before checks cover preparation ordering and both layouts.
- SARIF regressions include the issue's analysis-success/finding fixture and incomplete scans. Native tests cover transitive host/build coordinates, malformed graphs, provider refusal, unknown packages, missing credentials across all events and both project layouts. Integration tests verify failed security jobs fail the existing terminal gate. Packaging tests verify that this native NuGet package has no NuGet dependencies; an unrelated managed project was not added.

### Validation

- Full local script suite: **409 passed**, including 137 focused security/workflow/build tests.
- Debug, Release, ASan/UBSan and coverage: 10/10 C++ tests each; line/function coverage 100%, branches 93.3%.
- clang-format, clang-tidy, cppcheck, all five consumer examples, Doxygen, required documentation/file-size checks, actionlint with shellcheck, and regular/selected pedantic zizmor: passed.
- Real pip-audit resolution: 49 packages, no known vulnerabilities or skipped packages. Real native resolution retains all six library/build-tool coordinates, including the CPM bootstrap version and integrity hash. Explicit pipx workflow tools are included in the Python audit.
- All five workflows passed on final commit `f4120bd19ea507263616885938485dbeb84625d4`: [CI/CD](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40964476192), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40964476288), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40964476300), [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40964476177), [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/40964476214). Runs were created at 22:15:38 UTC after the 22:15:31 UTC commit on 2026-10-29. Local checks completed before commit/push; the working tree is clean and contains current `main` (`7ac7513`).
- Final C++ SARIF: 19 successful extractions, zero extractor failures, zero findings, and no warning/error diagnostics. All five project translation units and the public header are successfully extracted. Both C++ and Actions SARIF pass the unchanged strict validator; CI Python artifacts independently confirm 49 audited packages.

### Native provider setup and coverage

This repository has no `CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER` secret. Native coverage is explicitly **incomplete**, never reported as clean. Configure a free token from [Conan Audit registration](https://audit.conan.io/register) as documented in `docs/ci-cd.md`. Until configured, PRs warn and retain the inventory; main, scheduled and manual security runs fail with setup instructions. Once configured, provider refusals, unknown/unscanned packages (including unsupported vcpkg helpers or CPM), missing verdicts and vulnerabilities fail on every event. Both the setup policy and fatal provider verdicts have automated coverage. No authenticated clean native scan is claimed.

Three patch changelog fragments prepare the existing automatic release flow; the source version is intentionally left for that flow to bump.

body:
Fix the workflow stability defects in #5 and the NuGet authorization and trusted-publishing gaps in #6 in this single PR.

The old NuGet preflight treated creation of a verification key as proof that an API key could publish the configured package. The suggested temporary-key check alone also misses a wrong package glob: NuGet replaces that glob with the requested ID when creating the temporary key. Preflight now verifies the original publishing key as well, so a key whose glob or owner forbids the package cannot be reported as verified.

## Changes

- Pin all 27 literal runner labels and the full compiler matrix to `ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-15` and `windows-2025`, with repository-wide policy tests.
- Hash-pin lychee and zizmor, retain version comments and Dependabot updates, and remove their zizmor tag-pin exemptions.
- Configure Git's initial branch before checkout in `workflows.yml`; enforce the same configuration in all five active workflows.
- Complete the NuGet verification flow: create a temporary key with `Content-Length: 0`, find an existing published version through the public index, consume the temporary key with `GET /api/v2/verifykey/{id}/{version}`, then verify the original API key at the same endpoint. Both verification calls must return 200. HTTP 401/403 fails; missing versions, 404, malformed responses, rate limits and network uncertainty remain `unknown`.
- Support trusted publishing in both automatic and instant release jobs through hash-pinned `NuGet/login`, job-scoped permission to issue OIDC tokens and `vars.NUGET_USER`. Pass the temporary API-key output to the existing masked push command. Leave `NUGET_USER` unset to use the existing secret fallback; login failures stop the release.
- Report the selected authentication mode, keep opt-in HTTP diagnostics free of keys, and update setup instructions, including NuGet policies for renamed multi-language workflow files.
- Add a patch changelog fragment; the release pipeline performs the version bump.

## Requirements and research

The [complete requirement-by-requirement analysis](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/issue-7-497d9113d746/docs/case-studies/issue-7/README.md) lists every requirement from #5, #6 and #7, solution plans, alternatives, existing components, verified action hashes and limits. Both reported issues were reproduced and addressed; none is deferred. The audit covers all five active workflows, both publishing jobs, scripts, tests and current documentation. Historical workflow snapshots remain research evidence.

[NuGetGallery's CredentialBuilder](https://github.com/NuGet/NuGetGallery/blob/2f271fb8651906ecd841d0a658f9afc670e7021d/src/NuGetGallery.Services/Authentication/CredentialBuilder.cs#L71-L101) explains why temporary-key success cannot establish the original glob. Its [verification implementation](https://github.com/NuGet/NuGetGallery/blob/2f271fb8651906ecd841d0a658f9afc670e7021d/src/NuGetGallery/Controllers/ApiController.cs#L383-L414) accepts ordinary push keys and checks their original scopes. The same behavior was checked in current upstream source. Research also covers the official [trusted-publishing setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/nuget-org/trusted-publishing), [NuGet/login](https://github.com/NuGet/login), runner/action policies and related Interfaces PR #151. The solution reuses pytest, the local HTTP fixture, Python's standard library, actionlint/shellcheck and zizmor without a new production dependency.

## Reproduction and validation

The smallest remaining wrong-glob reproducer is `test_temporary_key_cannot_prove_original_package_glob`: POST and temporary-key verification return 200, but the original key is refused with 401/403. Before the correction, the seven new or strengthened focused cases failed; the fixed script rejects the denied credential and preserves unknown results. No live publishing credential or package push is needed.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q scripts/tests/test_preflight_credentials.py -k temporary_key_cannot
python3 -m pytest -q scripts/tests
```

Local validation:

- **306 script tests** passed; **94 focused preflight/publisher/workflow tests** passed.
- C++ Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan: **10 tests passed in each preset**.
- Pinned clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck; all five consumer examples passed.
- Pinned actionlint Docker image with shellcheck, shellcheck on both release scripts, both zizmor audit passes, required documentation, file-size and whitespace checks passed.

GitHub CI passed on final commit `b7917b2aec70b6e0a2d479c9636ef1d39f20ee46`: all five runs started at `2026-10-07T07:22:38Z`, after the commit at `07:22:32Z`. There are **28 passing checks, 5 expected skips, and no pending or failing checks**: [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37586939749), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37586939746), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37586939702), [Docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37586939678), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/37586939705). The workflow logs contain no Git default-branch hints or Ubuntu migration notice. The PR merge ref has **zero open code-scanning alerts**. Logs are preserved locally in `ci-logs/` and `experiments/issue-7/`.

Trusted publishing requires the documented nuget.org policy and `NUGET_USER` configuration. Deferred OIDC exchange and first-push scope are reported as unknown, preserving the existing verdict rules. Explicit runner labels fix OS generations while GitHub continues updating their tools; the macOS capacity notice is external.

Reverified at 2026-10-07 07:39 UTC on unchanged commit `b7917b2`: all **306 script tests**, C++ Debug/Release/ASan/UBSan (10 tests per preset), all five consumer examples, pinned C++ lint, actionlint/shellcheck, both zizmor passes and documentation/size/whitespace checks passed again. A fresh replay against `main` and the temporary-key-only implementation reproduced the wrong-glob false positive; the current implementation rejected both 401 and 403. Fresh CI logs match this head and contain no Git initial-branch hint or Ubuntu migration notice. GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` API explicitly recognizes **#5, #6 and #7**. All 22 requirements and their alternatives/implementation plans are mapped in the linked case study. Current official documentation, NuGetGallery source and all three action hashes were checked again. Both sub-issues are already fully implemented on this head; no further source changes are needed. `main` is already included in the branch and the working tree is clean. Fresh logs are preserved in `ci-logs/restart-3/` and `experiments/issue-7/*restart-3.log`.
